beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The first major proposal distinguishes several ways that something can exist.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A theorem may establish an object within a specified mathematical theory.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A computation may construct a representation under actual implementation conditions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Physical existence requires appropriate observational and causal grounds beyond that construction.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The text also considers processes, phenomena, and collectives that persist through change.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its challenge is to define rules that prevent invalid movement between these modes.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A taxonomy alone would not meet the programme’s own mathematical standard.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The reader can examine whether explicit typing changes inference, rather than merely naming differences.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An outfinite process begins with a finite specification and realized finite traces.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The relevant rule may allow extension without declaring a completed infinite totality.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Actual continuation still depends on resources, observations, and the surrounding context.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The frontier records where the present justification or realization reaches its boundary.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A bounded search can find no counterexample within the states it explored.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That outcome does not automatically establish safety for every possible execution.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book asks how frontier information can participate in further reasoning.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The interesting object is the justified extension, not simply a larger search counter.
